header:
How Uber makes
money on a ride

lines.text: Uber says it kept 21% of rider payments in Q3 2025. A 2026 study says over 50% in the US.
lines.say: Uber says it keeps twenty-one percent. A study says over half.

lines.text: First, the size: in 2025, riders and eaters booked $193 billion on Uber, and Uber recorded $52 billion in revenue.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, users booked a hundred ninety-three billion dollars on Uber; its revenue was fifty-two billion.

lines.text: On a ride, the rider pays an upfront fare. The driver gets a separate upfront offer. Uber keeps the gap, minus insurance and fees.
lines.say: On a ride, the rider pays an upfront fare. The driver gets a separate upfront offer. Uber keeps the gap, minus insurance and fees.

lines.text: How big is the gap? Uber says its take was 21% worldwide in Q3 2025. A Columbia professor's study with GigU says US take rates topped 50%.
lines.say: How big is the gap? Uber says its take was twenty-one percent worldwide in the third quarter of twenty twenty-five. A Columbia professor's study with Gig U says US take rates topped fifty percent.

lines.text: The study points to upfront pricing, launched in 2022, which set rider prices and driver pay separately.
lines.say: The study points to upfront pricing, launched in twenty twenty-two, which set rider prices and driver pay separately.

lines.text: Hypothetical $25 ride: at 21%, Uber keeps $5.25. At 50%, it keeps $12.50.
lines.say: Take a hypothetical twenty-five dollar ride. At twenty-one percent, Uber keeps five twenty-five. At fifty percent, twelve fifty.

lines.text: Either way, rides are Uber's profit engine: Mobility adjusted EBITDA was about $7.9 billion in 2025.
lines.say: Either way, rides are Uber's profit engine. Mobility adjusted EBITDA was about seven point nine billion dollars in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: Uber says it keeps 21% of fares. A study says over 50%
post.ig:
Uber says it kept 21% of rider payments worldwide in Q3 2025. A 2026 study says its US take topped 50%.

In 2025, Uber had $193B in gross bookings and $52B in revenue.
Riders pay an upfront fare; drivers get a separate upfront offer; Uber keeps the gap, minus insurance and fees. The study (Columbia's Len Sherman with GigU) points to upfront pricing, launched in 2022.
Hypothetical $25 ride: $5.25 at 21%, $12.50 at 50%.
Mobility adjusted EBITDA: about $7.9B in 2025.

Sources: Uber FY2025 results; Uber; Columbia/GigU study via Fast Company (2026).
News and education, not financial advice.
